about: Every miss of the first run on the fresh corpus (results/first.json, the frozen scanner), by cause. Read after that run, by the scanner's author. No label was changed.

A.cause: one BashOperator per model, made in a for-loop over the nodes of a manifest.json read at parse time. The reason names the HOME variable in the same command rather than the loop, which is misleading

B.reported_as: nothing (2, as a string command); unknown (1, as a list)
B.cause: a DockerOperator whose image's entrypoint is dbt, given only the sub-command and its flags: command='run --target dev', or ['run', '--project-dir', '/dbt']
B.follow_up: the 2 silent links are unknowns after the freeze (08c6ee6); LP-245

C.cause: a repo-local operator subclass, DbtDockerOperator, that builds its own dbt command

D.cause: the task is inside if os.getenv('DBT_ENABLED', 'false').lower() == 'true': the evaluator took the default as the value, decided the test was false, and skipped the branch in silence
D.follow_up: reported as unknowns after the freeze (08c6ee6); LP-246

E.cause: cmds=['bash', '-cx'] is not recognised as a shell

F.cause: the pod's command is in its pod_template_file, a YAML file outside the DAG files
F.follow_up: none: out of reach of a scanner of DAG files

G.cause: dbt test: the project's only tests are in YAML under test-paths, which the stand-in manifest does not read

entry_fixes_seen: One of the 15 correct links went through an Entry fix: cd $AIRFLOW_HOME/restaurant_analytis, matched by the path after the variable (LP-0o1). The 0.2.0 scanner linked it too, through its only-project fallback, so the correct links are the same 15 (results/baseline-0.2.0.json). No link here needs a container mount or the only-project fallback for a container path (LP-c05), and no imported helper builds an operator (LP-z2x). This corpus therefore does not measure the Entry fixes; their fixtures and the first corpus (in-sample) do.
